body.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\),
\(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\).  Along every growth array with
\(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), the total interval \(C_\alpha\)
in \texttt{def:honest-interval} satisfies
\[
 \liminf
 \inf_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \inf_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \{\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\in C_\alpha\}
 \ge1-\alpha,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)]
 \le CR_\star^{1/2}.
\]
These conclusions use no lower local-modulus condition, count the full-range
interval on every declared bad-sample branch, and never divide by an
estimated variance.  If \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\), every single
data-measurable random interval \(I_\alpha\) having the same uniform
fixed-query-kernel coverage obeys
\[
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)]
 \ge cR_\star^{1/2}
\]
for all sufficiently large indices.  On the fixed-query
independent-calendar subclasses, both upper and lower spacing terms are
\(T^{-\lambda/d}\).  The theorem makes no higher-order claim for
\(\lambda>1\).

For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its labelled regular
conditional kernel is in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost
every query under the marginal law of \(z_0\), and
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) there.  Therefore the coverage and
expected-length upper conclusions apply to \(P(\cdot\mid z_0)\) at those
query values.  No claim is made about a chosen conditional version at a null
query.
body.justification: The interval is one observable-data rule that concentrates whole bounded unit histories and adds Holder and full-covariance donor radii.
body.gap: Armstrong--Kolesar ordinary-regression intervals and Cattaneo--Feng--Titiunik dependent synthetic-control prediction do not give this generated-query interval or its donor expected-length converse.
body.consumer: The procedure is conditionally honest without calendar-score decoupling and transfers to causal panel laws only on their marginal-conull query set.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\) and a labelled point
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Boundedness gives
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\in[-2B,2B]\).  On the regular branch \(r=0\).  Conditional on the exact design and donor sample, the selected weights are response-independent, nonnegative, and satisfy \(\sum_tw_{st}=1\).  Define one variable per complete unit history by
\[
 \zeta_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\left[
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s
 -\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}\right].           \tag{1}
\]
Donor--panel independence means that further conditioning on donors does not change the conditional unit-history law given the design.  The two centering clauses in Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} center (1), and its cross-unit condition makes these variables independent across \((s,i)\).  Their range lengths are at most
\[
 d_{si}=\frac{2B\pi_s}{n_s}
 \left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right).                         \tag{2}
\]
For a variable \(V\in[a,b]\), convexity of the exponential gives
\(\mathbb E\exp\{u(V-\mathbb EV)\}\le
\exp\{u^2(b-a)^2/8\}\).  Multiplication over the independent variables, exponential Markov, and optimization in \(u\), followed by the definitions of \(A_w,M_w\), imply
\[
 \Pr\left\{\left|\sum_{s,i}\zeta_{si}\right|>r_{\mathrm{unit}}
 \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal X,(Z_j)_j\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}.                                     \tag{3}
\]
The positive linear term in \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) only enlarges this radius.  The argument treats one entire unit history as one bounded variable and uses no calendar-score independence.

Put \(q=Sd\).  Spectral clipping gives
\(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I_q\).  Every fold has size at least \(N/3\), so donor unbiasedness and
\(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_q\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\left[
 N\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2^2\right]
 \le\frac{6qC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.                              \tag{4}
\]
This uses only the deterministic lower eigenvalue after clipping; it does not require independence of the sample mean and covariance estimate.  Markov's inequality, a union bound over at most two folds, and the definition of \(q_{\mathrm{don}}\) imply
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_\ell
 \|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2
 >q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.                                    \tag{5}
\]
On the complement, \(\widehat\Sigma\preceq2C_\Sigma I_q\) and projection contraction imply
\(\max_\ell\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2\le CN^{-1/2}\).

At a selected local-constant fit, nonnegative unit-mass weights and kernel support give
\[
 \left|\sum_tw_{st}^{(\ell)}m_s(X_{st})
       -m_s(\widetilde z_{\ell s})\right|
 \le C\{\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
          +\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda\}.                       \tag{6}
\]
Holder continuity from \(\widetilde z_{\ell s}\) to \(z_{0s}\), (5), and the defining domination by \(C_H\) bound the deterministic error by
\(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Combining (3), (5), and
\(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha\) proves coverage on the regular branch.  Every declared bad branch returns \([-2B,2B]\), which contains the target.  Intersecting a covering interval with this known range preserves coverage.  Thus the coverage probability is at least \(1-\alpha\) for every non-fallback index and equals one on a fallback branch; in particular it implies the displayed uniform asymptotic coverage.

For expected length, on the regular branch \(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\).  Therefore, with \(A=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\),
\[
 r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}
 \le C(\alpha,B)A^{1/2},                                       \tag{7}
\]
where \(\max_s\pi_s/n_s\le A^{1/2}\).  Let
\(\mathcal G=\{h_s^\star<1\text{ for every }s\}\).  On \(\mathcal G\), certificate optimality at the feasible reference pair
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\), together with the bandwidth floor, gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{bias}}
 \le C\sum_s\pi_s\left\{(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\right\}.                \tag{8}
\]
Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, projection contraction, and Jensen yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\le CN^{-\lambda/2}.      \tag{9}
\]
The interval length is always at most \(4B\).  Since \(0<h_s^\star\le1\), a union bound and Markov's inequality give
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal G^c)\le\sum_s\mathbb E(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}.    \tag{10}
\]
Apply Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} to (8)--(10).  Uniformly over all fixed queries and labelled points,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)
 \le C\bigg[&A^{1/2}
 +\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\\
 &+\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}
 +N^{-\lambda/2}\bigg]+CR_\star.
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{11}
\]
All observed coordinates are finite under boundedness, every search is over a compact set or a finite grid with a deterministic fallback, and spectral clipping is total.  Thus the undefined-or-nonfinite branch has probability zero.  The conditions \(N<2\) and \(n_s<2\) disappear eventually along the stated growth arrays.  The final term in (11) charges the full interval on \(\mathcal G^c\): by (10), the anchor second-moment bound, fixed positive cohort weights, and fixed \(S\), that contribution is at most \(CR_\star\).  Since \(R_\star\to0\) along the growth array, \(R_\star\le R_\star^{1/2}\) eventually.  The smoothing domination in Theorem \texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram} now gives
\[
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)
 \le CR_\star^{1/2}.                                           \tag{12}
\]
In the independent-calendar subclass, the anchor lemma replaces the logarithmic term by \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).

For the converse, suppose two observed laws with targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) have a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta>2\alpha\).  Uniform coverage \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under both laws gives
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I_\alpha\}
 \ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).                                        \tag{13}
\]
Every interval on this event has length at least
\(|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)
 \ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.                \tag{14}
\]
For any two laws, take the dominating measure \(\vartheta=P_0+P_1\) and define
\(d\nu=\min\{dP_0/d\vartheta,dP_1/d\vartheta\}\,d\vartheta\).  Then
\(\nu\le P_0,P_1\) and its total mass is
\(1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), so every total-variation overlap bound below supplies the common submeasure required in (13).

The treated pair used in the marginal proof can have common mass arbitrarily close to one by reducing its fixed \(\gamma\); it yields \(cA^{1/2}\).  For the donor channel, apply Lemma \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} with \(\eta\in(2\alpha,1)\).  Use a common independent uniform design and, in the displaced cohort, the common regression
\[
 m(x)=b_0+a_0|x_k-z_k^{(0)}|^\lambda,                            \tag{15}
\]
with constant regressions elsewhere, deterministic responses
\(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\), a common positive treated wealth, and untreated event wealth \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\) under alternative \(v\).  Small \(a_0,b_0\) verify support and Holder smoothness.  Because the displacement has one coordinate and
\(N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z^{(1)}-z^{(0)})\|_2^2=c_\eta^2\), ellipticity gives coordinate separation at least
\(c_\eta c_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}\).  The panel coordinates coincide, the donor laws have common mass at least \(\eta\), and (15) makes the targets differ by at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\); thus (14) gives the donor lower bound.

Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies, in one fixed-query class, common mass above \(2\alpha\) and separation
\(c\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\).  Equation (14), followed by smoothing domination, gives \(cR_\star^{1/2}\).  In the independent-calendar class, choose the no-hit cube in (8) of the marginal proof small enough that its common mass exceeds \(2\alpha\); this gives \(cT^{-\lambda/d}\).  These three pairs prove the uniformly honest expected-length converse for every one observable-data interval selected before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\).

For a panel law, membership of its labelled regular conditional point and the equality
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau\) hold on the marginal-conull query set established in Theorem \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} and Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification}.  Applying (3)--(12) there proves the causal transfer and makes no assertion at a query-null value.
